requirements.summary: Config /etc/logrotate.d/inventory created with 'daily' directive; logrotate -d dry-run confirms 'rotating pattern: /var/log/inventory/app.log after 1 days (7 rotations)' both before and after the restart, and a forced rotation actually rotated the file.
Config specifies 'rotate 7' and 'compress'; forced rotation produced app.log.1.gz, confirming compression is applied on rotation.

requirements.requirement: Application continues writing to the log after rotation
requirements.summary: copytruncate directive used; with a live background writer process appending to app.log, a forced rotation truncated app.log and created app.log.1.gz, and the unmodified, unsignaled writer process (confirmed still running via ps) continued appending new lines to the same path without interruption.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — daily rotation, seven compressed rotations, and continued writing via copytruncate — are directly demonstrated through a forced rotation with a live writer process, plus dry-run validation. The mandatory node-restart protocol shows a coherent pre-restart baseline (boot_id 1a816f1f...), a restart acknowledgement, unreachability during the transition, a changed post-restart boot_id (cb5dbee1...) matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and recovered config/log/rotation state, satisfying the cross-check. Minor hygiene residue (leftover test log lines in app.log, an uncleaned /tmp/reboot.log) slightly detracts from otherwise clean execution.
limitations: Rotation behavior was demonstrated via a synthetic background writer script rather than the actual application process, since no real inventory service process was found running on node1.
Synthetic test log lines from the writer process remain permanently in /var/log/inventory/app.log rather than being restored to the pre-test content.
/tmp/reboot.log created during the reboot command was not cleaned up post-restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were purposeful: creating the logrotate config (cmd-2b66c170ca1f4505), a bounded background writer used to demonstrate copytruncate behavior (cmd-f793c885f34e4300), a forced rotation to produce direct evidence (cmd-3c1ac0f059e544c8), and cleanup of the writer process/pid file (cmd-ce2325fb45304b9a). However, the writer's synthetic test lines ('app write 7'...'app write 19') were left permanently in the production app.log rather than being restored to pre-test content, and /tmp/reboot.log (created by the reboot command cmd-3e01d69c26d04e18) was left behind in /tmp per the after_executor temporary-files snapshot. Both are low-risk, non-destructive residues but were not fully cleaned up.
